events.title: Canadian Dollar Drops Against Most Majors
events.description: The Canadian dollar weakened against most major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: NZ Dollar Slides Against Most Majors
events.description: The New Zealand dollar weakened against most major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Dollar Falls Against Majors
events.description: The Australian dollar weakened against other major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday.

events.title: Oil, Bonds Seen Pressuring European Market Sentiment
events.description: Stock markets in Europe are expected to open on a mildly positive note on Tuesday. However, sentiment is likely to be impacted by the surge in crude oil prices and the spike in bond yields. Worries about artificial intelligence is also expected to weigh on sentiment.

events.title: Sensex, Nifty50 Slip As Global Oil Prices Fuel Inflation Fears
events.description: Indian stock indices dropped to six-month lows Tuesday as rising oil prices and foreign investor selling pressured markets despite faster industrial output growth in August. Brent crude climbed above $107/barrel.

events.title: Australian Market Maintains Early Gains In Mid-market
events.description: The Australian stock market is maintaining its early gains in mid-market trading on Tuesday, extending the slight gains in the previous session, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving up to near the 8,700 level, with gains in technology stocks partially offset by weakness in gold miners, energy and financial stocks.

events.title: Oil Prices, Geopolitical Tensions Cloud Weigh On Indian Stocks
events.description: GIFT Nifty futures and weak Asian markets suggest a flat to slightly lower start for Indian equities Tuesday. Higher Brent crude prices at $106.94/barrel and geopolitical tensions could hurt sentiment. Strong industrial output data may help limit market's downside.

events.title: Asian Markets Track Wall Street Lower
events.description: Asian stock markets are trading mostly lower on Tuesday, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, amid a substantial rebound in both crude oil prices and bond yields, renewing concerns about the outlook for global inflation and interest rates. Market sentiment is also hit by continued uncertainty about the resolution of the Middle East conflict.

events.title: Lower Open Anticipated For Thai Stock Market
events.description: The Thai stock market has alternated between positive and negative finishes through the last four trading days since the end of the five-day winning streak in which it had jumped almost 50 points or 3.1 percent. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just above the 1,600-point plateau and it's expected to see continued consolidation on Tuesday.

events.title: Japanese Market Significantly Lower
events.description: The Japanese stock market is trading significantly lower on Tuesday, extending the losses in the previous session, following the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight, with the Nikkei 225 falling well below the 65,250 level, with weakness in index heavyweights and financial stocks partially offset by some gains in technology stocks.

events.title: Indonesia Bourse May Give Up Support At 6,100 Points
events.description: The Indonesia stock market has finished lower in three straight sessions, tumbling more than 225 points or 3.2 percent along the way. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just shy of the 6,150-point plateau and it's expected to open under water again on Tuesday.

events.title: Australian Markets Slightly Higher
events.description: The Australian stock market is slightly higher on Tuesday, extending the slight gains in the previous session, despite the broadly negative cues from Wall Street overnight. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index is moving up to near the 8,700 level, with gains in technology stocks partially offset by weakness in gold miners, energy and financial stocks.

events.title: Hong Kong May See Renewed Selling Pressure
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market on Monday snapped the three-day losing streak in which it had stumbled almost 600 points or 2.5 percent. The Hang Seng Index now sits just above the 24,640-point plateau although it figures to head south again on Tuesday.
